title: line_rate_bps maps capacity==0 to the maximum rate (799,920,000 bps -> "800 Mbps") instead of 0
detail: Zero-capacity input takes transit_ticks' div-by-0 branch (returns 1), so the derived rate is the transit-1 maximum — a dead link/node reads "800 Mbps". Sibling new procs (util_pct_window, served_to_octets) zero-guard; line_rate_bps and line_rate_bytes_per_tick (returns 1500) do not.
recommended_fix: Guard capacity == 0 -> return 0 in line_rate_bps and line_rate_bytes_per_tick (mirroring util_pct_window), and/or validate node_types throughput_units > 0 at catalog load.

title: Tick-0 sentinel collision: work recorded at tick 0 is never counted by bundle_tx_window (slot key 0 == "never written")
detail: At tick 0 the record writes tx_served but `0 != 0` is false, so the key stays 0 — the sentinel; the window test `st > lo` (0 > 0) then never counts it. step's guard admits a first step at tick 0 (`tick < state.tick` only latches backward); all current callers start at tick 1.
recommended_fix: Store tick+1 as the slot key (0 stays a true "never" sentinel), adjusting bundle_tx_record and the window comparison accordingly.

title: Same-tick re-step accumulates each execution's served units into one slot, over-reporting tx_octets and pre-clamp utilization
detail: step() deliberately permits same-tick re-steps (documented for drop_sites/events); the ring has no per-execution clear, so a re-stepped tick's slot sums both executions' work — tx_octets over-reports and windowed util exceeds the one-tick budget (clamped at 100).
recommended_fix: Reset the bundle's current-tick slot at the top of flow_step's serve pass (per-execution), keeping the tick-key rewrite only for stale slots.
